reference_title: Drilled Shafts: Construction Procedures and LRFD Design Methods

sections.title: Responsibilities
sections.body: Inspection and documentation of drilled shaft construction is critically important. Unlike driven piles, drilled shaft performance can only be assessed by verifying installation conformance with contract documents, approved Installation Plan, and procedures used for successful technique and test shafts. Inspector role: monitor construction process; maintain records; provide timely information to designer and owner on unanticipated conditions and deviations. Inspector does NOT direct construction — only contractor has authority to direct operations. Inspector must be qualified by training and experience; NHI Course No. 132070 certification recommended; should have prior experience or work under supervision until qualified. Inspector roles and responsibilities: attend pre-construction and construction meetings; attend safety training; be familiar with site conditions, subsurface conditions, contract documents, approved Installation Plan, installation criteria and tolerances; have all inspection equipment calibrated and in good order; observe and document all drilled shaft activities; observe slurry testing; observe concrete field testing and sample cylinders; immediately inform designer, resident engineer, or owner of any unanticipated conditions or non-conforming work; measure and record quantities for payment. Inspector should share observations with contractor to allow timely resolution — but may not direct operations. Contractor responsibilities: determine means and methods conforming to contract documents; install per approved Installation Plan consistent with technique shaft procedures; responsible for structural integrity of completed shafts.
key_points: Inspector monitors and records — does NOT direct contractor operations
Inspector must be qualified; NHI Course No. 132070 certification recommended
Inspector must immediately notify designer/engineer of any non-conforming work or unexpected conditions
Inspector should share observations with contractor for timely resolution
Contractor is responsible for installed structural integrity of completed shafts

sections.title: Inspection Activities
sections.body: Inspector observes all stages: set-up through completion of concrete placement including casing removal. Set-Up checklist: attend pre-construction meetings; collect all project documents; verify equipment calibrated; check measurement equipment (measuring tape, weighted sounding tape, 4-ft level, carpenter's square, slurry testing equipment, concrete testing equipment, concrete molds); coordinate with surveying for control elevations and shaft locations. Casing inspection: verify casing OD and minimum wall thickness; check for excessive deformation or out-of-roundness; record casing lengths and segments; inspect cutting teeth. Drilling fluid inspection: record type of fluid; measure and record slurry properties during excavation and prior to concrete placement (Marsh Funnel, density, pH, sand content, temperature); verify slurry meets specification requirements. Drilled shaft excavation inspection: observe excavation progress and record materials encountered; note caving, seepage, and groundwater conditions; measure and record excavation depth at completion; observe base cleanout; measure and record sediment depth after cleanout (requirements typically: dry hole ≤2 in.; wet hole ≤1.5 in. for side shear critical or ≤2.5 in. for end bearing critical); use downhole camera or SID when specified. Reinforcement placement: inspect cage for compliance with drawings (bar size, spacing, cover, splice lengths); verify integrity of CSL/TIP access tubes; verify cage positioned at correct elevation; record cage installation. Concrete placement: measure concrete volume for each truckload; record slump (or slump flow for SCC) and temperature for each truck; collect and label concrete cylinders; monitor concrete level rise (calculate from volume); record tremie insertion depth; record casing extraction depth and speed; observe and record completion of concrete placement. Completed drilled shaft: record final shaft top elevation; observe for any anomalous concrete consumption suggesting cavities; record construction log.
key_points: Record slurry properties: Marsh Funnel, density, pH, sand content during excavation AND before concrete
Sediment depth limits: dry hole ≤2 in.; wet hole ≤1.5 in. (side shear critical) or ≤2.5 in. (end bearing critical)
Measure and record concrete volume per truck; track concrete level rise vs. theoretical
Record slump/slump flow and temperature for each concrete truck
Collect and label concrete cylinders per specification
Downhole camera or SID when required by contract or when conditions are questionable

sections.title: Common Problems
sections.body: Common construction problems to watch for: (1) Base cleanliness — loose sediment, cuttings, or slurry cake at base; verify by sounding after cleanout; use downhole camera in questionable cases; (2) Concrete volume anomalies — significant excess suggests cavity or overbreak outside casing; significant shortfall suggests necking, concrete loss, or improper placement; (3) Cage flotation — rebar cage floated upward during concrete placement from concrete buoyancy forces; prevent by adequate ballasting or holding cage during concrete pour; (4) Concrete slump/workability loss before placement complete — can cause arching in casing, poor flow through cage, cage distortion; (5) Slurry contamination at concrete surface — slurry or sediment inclusions at top of concrete; remove laitance and contaminated concrete after placement; (6) Drilling into recently concreted adjacent shaft — vibrations disturb fresh concrete; maintain proper sequence; (7) Casing extraction problems — casing stuck due to concrete set or excessive drag; concrete arching; (8) Misalignment — shaft center exceeds tolerance; verify plan position during setup.
key_points: Monitor concrete volume continuously — anomalies indicate cavities or necking
Cage flotation: prevent by ballasting cage or holding during pour
Slump/workability loss during placement: major risk for casing extraction operations
Remove laitance and contaminated concrete at top after placement
Drilling sequence near recently placed concrete: maintain adequate spacing/time

sections.title: Records and Forms
sections.body: Complete written documentation essential for communicating construction activities and providing permanent record. Records provide primary means for identification and initial assessment of potential problems. Records also needed for assessing differing site condition (DSC) claims. Required records for each shaft: shaft identifier and location (coordinates, station, offset); planned and actual shaft diameter; planned and actual tip elevation; ground surface elevation; date and time of excavation start and completion; materials encountered (with depth intervals); groundwater depth; casing details (length, diameter, type, set depth); drilling fluid details and properties (type, measurements at intervals, measurements before concrete); base cleanout method and final sediment depth; downhole camera/SID observations (if used); reinforcing cage details (lengths, splice locations, access tube details); concrete pour details (start/stop time, truck tickets, slump/slump flow, temperature, volume, cylinder sample numbers); concrete volume plot (cumulative poured vs. theoretical); any anomalies or deviations noted; signature of inspector. Volume plot: plot of cumulative concrete volume poured vs. theoretical volume (based on shaft dimensions) as concrete is poured — real-time QC tool showing overfill (cavities) or shortfall (necking).
key_points: Complete records required for each shaft — permanent project documentation
Records provide basis for DSC claim evaluation
Concrete volume plot: cumulative poured vs. theoretical — real-time QC tool
Volume excess indicates cavities/overbreak; volume shortfall indicates necking or concrete loss
Inspector signature required on all forms

sections.title: Summary
sections.body: Chapter provided guidance on inspection roles, responsibilities, and activities for drilled shaft construction. Inspector monitors and documents construction without directing operations. Complete written records for each shaft are essential for QA, performance assessment, and DSC claim evaluation. References: NHI Course No. 132070 (2002); ADSC/DFI 'Drilled Shaft Inspector's Manual' 2nd Edition (2004).
